subject: Re: Peregrine - GPU blend, burst capacity and reservation clarifications
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@peregrine.ai>

Cc: Rajesh Malhotra <rajesh.malhotra@peregrine.ai>, Procurement <procurement@peregrine.ai>

Subject: Peregrine RFP - follow up on GPU blend and burst sizing

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the product overview this week. Peregrine is putting together the RFP response pack for our internal engineering and procurement reviews. We had a couple of detailed follow-ups from our infra team around dedicated capacity: specifically, they want clarity on recommended GPU mixes for a mixed workload (real-time chat gen at p50 60ms, batching for embeddings, and occasional long-context summarization jobs), how burst capacity behaves against reservations, and how quantized model variants change the packing/throughput math.

Attached is the questionnaire we started filling out (peregrine_rfp-questionnaire.pdf). Can you or someone on your team provide a worked example: a 200 vCPU / 40k daily-user throughput target with 6M tokens/day and a 10% long-context tail (8k tokens), and show recommended reservation tiers (1/3/6/12 month), GPU types, and expected steady-state vs burst TPS? A line-item on pre-warm / cold-start seconds per GPU would also be great.

Procurement is on a tight cadence and would like a workbook we can drop numbers into rather than just prose. Is there a simple workbook you can share?

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Chief Infrastructure Officer
Peregrine Analytics

--

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine RFP - follow up on GPU blend and burst sizing

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the detailed ask and the questionnaire. We're happy to provide a worked example and a small workbook so your team can swap in their traffic assumptions. I've looped in Karthik (product infra lead) and Marcus (capacity planning) who prepared a short workbook and a few clarifying questions below.

High-level clarifications before we model:
- When you say "real-time chat gen at p50 60ms" — is that token-latency budget at p50 across your end-to-end stack (incl network), or strictly model inference p50? We usually size for model p50 ~20-40ms depending on model family and quantization.
- For "batching for embeddings", are embeddings used for nightly re-indexing (large batch jobs) or near-real-time similarity calls? That affects whether we recommend dedicated reserved nodes for embeddings or use burst lanes.

We'll attach an initial workbook with three reservation scenarios (monthly, quarterly, annual) and run the numbers for: A100-80GB (fp16), H100-80GB (fp16), and an 8-bit quantized L4-style instance (Q8). The workbook will show token/s GPU and tokens/sec per GPU for short-context and long-context workloads, and a reservation/burst cost comparison.

Expect the workbook and a narrative by EOD Wednesday PST. If you have a target commitment band (e.g., $/month or committed vGPU-hours) that helps pick the most economical blend.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@peregrine.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine RFP - follow up on GPU blend and burst sizing

Samantha —

Attached is the initial workbook: redwood_gpu_mixer_workbook.xlsx (also shared to the Drive link below). Summary bullets from the workbook:

- Baseline assumptions used: 6M tokens/day, 10% long-tail (8k tokens), chat p50 model inference budget 25ms (quantized Q8), and embedding calls are 30% near-real-time, 70% nightly batch.
- Recommended steady-state reservation: a mixed fleet of 6 x H100-80GB reserved (for low-latency chat and long-context), 8 x A100-80GB reserved (for batching/throughput), and 10 x Q8-class vGPUs (packed on Ampere L4-style hardware) for pre-allocated low-cost inference (embedding near-real-time). This blend minimizes cost while keeping p50 latency targets.
- Burst lanes: We recommend a 30% burst buffer (on top of reserved capacity) using pre-warmed shared hosts that can be spun up in <90s for additional throughput and a hot-cache of model weights. For very short spikes (<60s), we rely on prefix KV cache on reserved nodes which absorbs token spikes without spinning new GPUs.
- Quantization impact: Q8 reduces tokens/sec per GPU for long-context due to KV cache bloat, but allows >2x packing density for short-context chat. We show both per-token cost and 95th-percentile latency tradeoffs in the workbook.

Open questions for Peregrine engineers:
1) Is the 25ms model p50 assumption acceptable for your UX? If you need ~10-15ms p50 then the H100 ratio should increase and the A100 reserved count reduce.
2) For procurement: do you require a single annual commitment, or would a hybrid (90-day ramp + annual baseline) be preferable? We can model both.

We can do a quick walkthrough of the workbook on Friday; propose 11:00am PST.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: Peregrine RFP - follow up on GPU blend and burst sizing

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the kind of workbook we needed. A couple quick clarifications before the walkthrough:

- The team confirms the 25ms model p50 is fine as a baseline but asks you to show a 15ms scenario so we can see delta in cost.
- Procurement prefers a hybrid: a 3-month ramp (quarterly) followed by a 12-month annual baseline. Please include the amortized discount tiers for the annual baseline in the workbook.
- Can you add a simple SLA paragraph about how burst capacity is honored during scheduled maintenance windows (we need to know any blackout windows where shared burst lanes cannot be used).

We'll take the 11:00am PST slot on Friday. Rajesh will join for the procurement Q&A.

Regards,
Samantha
